story_type: man alone abandons a boat as it sinks bow up, swimmer and basket hoist
hook: His boat went down nose first, twelve miles out.
narration: His boat went down nose first, twelve miles off the California coast.
He was alone on an eighteen foot boat, west of San Onofre State Beach.
At eleven twenty that morning, he called the Coast Guard. His boat was taking on water.
He waited for a tow. Then the boat started to sink, fast.
[short pause] At twelve forty five, he abandoned it and went into the water.
A Jayhawk crew from Sector San Diego arrived and lowered a rescue swimmer on the cable.
The swimmer's job is to reach the survivor in the water, so the survivor never has to swim to the helicopter.
Then the crew sent down the rescue basket.
He climbed in and rode it up to the door.
outcome: The crew hoisted him aboard and flew him to Sector San Diego with no reported injuries.

title: His boat sank nose first, 12 miles out
description:
On Nov. 6, 2017, a man abandoned his sinking 18-foot boat about 12 miles west of San Onofre State Beach, California, and a Coast Guard Jayhawk crew from Sector San Diego pulled him from the water.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Coast Guard Sector San Diego, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/563284/coast-guard-rescues-boater-sinking-vessel-near-san-onofre-state-beach
